literal: the cart points south, its tracks go north
meaning_long: doing things that take you further from your goal
source: 《战国策·魏策四》 (public domain), retold in our own words.
story: Ancient China, about 2,300 years ago. A rich man is racing in his chariot to the kingdom of Chu, which lies to the south, but his chariot is heading north. His wise friend Ji Liang stops him: 'Chu is south! Why are you going north?' The rich man laughs: 'My horse is very fast! I have plenty of money! My driver is the best!' Ji Liang sighs: the better all those things are, the farther he will end up from Chu.
continuity: - THE RICH MAN: plump, very confident man about 45, bushy black beard, tall black official hat, purple silk robe with gold trim, a big green jade ring, a huge grin.
- JI LIANG, the friend: thin, wise man about 50, short grey beard, calm worried eyes, plain grey-green robe, bamboo walking stick.
- THE CHARIOT: one two-wheeled wooden chariot pulled by one big, powerful white horse, driven by a young muscular driver (red headband, brown short jacket). The driver is always a small figure.
- SETTING: a long straight dusty road across flat open country with soft grey ink-wash mountains on the horizon; a plain wooden road post shaped like an arrow (no writing).
scenes: The twist (used as the hook, first frame of the video)

On the dusty road: the white horse gallops away to the RIGHT pulling the chariot at full speed, dust flying, the rich man waving back happily with a huge grin. In the foreground a plain wooden arrow-shaped road post clearly points the OPPOSITE way, to the LEFT. Ji Liang stands beside the post with one hand on his head in disbelief. Both faces clear. This is the most important image; the editor will push in on it.
The rich man stands proudly in his chariot as the big white horse gallops, cape and beard blowing in the wind, pointing forward like a hero. The young driver holds the reins. Dust cloud behind.

Ji Liang has stepped onto the road with his walking stick raised, stopping the chariot. He points back over his shoulder in the other direction. The horse rears slightly; the rich man leans over the side of the chariot, curious.
The rich man proudly pats the neck of his big powerful white horse, which tosses its mane, looking very fast and strong. Ji Liang looks on, unimpressed.
The rich man shakes open a heavy cloth purse spilling round bronze coins (plain, no characters), grinning widely. Ji Liang raises an eyebrow.
The rich man throws an arm around his young muscular driver, who flexes one arm proudly. Ji Liang facepalms in the background.

Wide shot from above: the chariot speeds north along the endless straight road, getting smaller and smaller, a long dust trail behind. Tiny Ji Liang stands far behind, looking the other way, toward the south.
The tracks (background for the big title)

Low close-up of the dusty road: two long wheel tracks and hoof prints running away into the distance in the lower half of the frame. The upper half is calm, plain sky with soft grey ink washes and almost nothing in it (we place the big title there). No people.

A modern street: the same RICH MAN (bushy black beard, big grin, jade ring) in a purple modern jacket carries a dozen shopping bags (plain, no logos) and proudly holds up an empty piggy bank. Beside him the same JI LIANG (short grey beard) in a grey-green cardigan facepalms. No text, no signs, no logos.
lines: Best horse, best driver, totally wrong direction.
A rich man was racing to the kingdom of Chu.
A friend stopped him: Chu is south! You're going north!
No problem! My horse is fast!
And my driver is the best!
So the faster he went, the farther he got.
The cart points south, the tracks go north.
It means your actions take you away from your goal.
Like saving money by buying everything on sale.
title: Best horse, best driver… totally wrong direction 🐎 | 南辕北辙
desc: 南辕北辙 (nán yuán běi zhé) = your actions take you away from your goal. Ever done that? 👇
pinned: 南 south · 辕 cart shafts · 北 north · 辙 tracks. 📝 想省钱却天天网购，真是南辕北辙。(Xiǎng shěng qián què tiāntiān wǎnggòu, zhēn shì nán yuán běi zhé.) = Wanting to save money but shopping online every day? That's heading north to reach the south.
